# Titan VK56 engine swap with auto trans

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> **Some safety-critical values on this page are not confirmed** (marked [Unverified] or [Partial]): they come from one source or are only partly supported. Verify against the factory service manual before use; later runs re-check them against new sources.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Lift the vehicle to access the underside and locate bolts A, B, and C on the valve body. [t286]

[Partial] Source a conversion harness made from the Titan's original wiring and combined with existing Xterra harnesses. [t286]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. [Partial] Remove the front end assembly as one large piece.
2. Leave the radiator, AC condenser, transmission cooler, fan, and power steering cooler intact on the crossmember.
3. [Partial] Remove the grill, bumper, and headlights.
4. Disconnect both transmission lines from the nipples just above the oil cooler to drain fluid into a bucket using cardboard ramps.
5. Remove the radiator drain plug on the underside of the driver's side end to allow coolant drainage while working elsewhere.
6. Disconnect the power steering hardline from the softlines on both the driver and passenger sides.
7. Use a tiny Phillips head screwdriver between the lines at the driver's side connection to break the hoses apart before removing the softline.
8. Place another piece of folded cardboard under the driver's side connection to guide reservoir fluid into a bucket in front of the truck.
9. Release the AC refrigerant by locating the high-pressure port near the front driver's side and inserting an Allen key that fits the valve.
10. Wrap a thick rag around the port with the Allen key sticking out, then wrap a plastic shopping bag over the rag to contain potential messes while wearing rubber gloves.
11. Stand upwind and press and release the Allen key quickly many times to gradually bleed off pressure as oily refrigerant escapes.
12. Disconnect the AC lines by separating the driver's side line from the radiator and the passenger side line from the firewall.
13. Remove both upper and lower radiator hoses from the radiator, then replace the plug in the bottom of the radiator.
14. [Partial] Connect a floor jack under the transmission to support its weight while disconnecting the wiring harness for the electric fan behind the cooler.
15. Disconnect the wiring harness going to the radiator thermo sensor located right by the transmission cooler fan harness.
16. Remove all 12 bolts holding the front crossmember in place, with six on each side.
17. [Partial] Walk backward slowly while carrying the heavy crossmember away from the truck until it is free.
18. Disconnect the engine wiring harness from the ECU by pushing in the locking lever and pulling the handle down.
19. [Partial] Locate the wire loom coming into the IPDM fuse box on the front passenger corner and disconnect two or three harnesses from it.
20. Find a thick wire loom clipped to a metal tab alongside both fuse boxes, then use a small flathead screwdriver at the backside indentation of its plastic clip.
21. Push that plastic tab in while pulling up on the loom to release it from the metal tab.
22. Follow that loose loom about 12 inches toward the engine and find where it attaches to another clip, then release it.
23. [Partial] Pull the harness completely out from underneath the smaller fuse box situated in front of the IPDM.
24. Remove the bolt holding the plastic leg of the smaller fusebox to the body so the loom can be maneuvered freely.
25. [Partial] Remove the 10mm bolt on a swivel with an extension that holds the metal plate underneath the fusebox to the body.
26. [Partial] Use needle-nose pliers or cut zip ties to release where the thick wire loom is clipped to the now-free metal plate.
27. Slide open the door of the IPDM box by pulling up and out on its clips, then wiggle the big thick loom out from underneath the smaller fusebox.
28. Disconnect the grounding wire going to the engine block.
29. [Partial] Remove both driver's side and passenger's side catalytic converters as they interfere with engine removal.
30. Pop off the power steering reservoir by pulling up on its mount with some elbow grease.
31. Squeeze a 10mm angled box wrench from behind between the steering rack and crossmember to remove the bolt holding the low-pressure soft line coupler under the oil filter ramp.
32. Disconnect the driver's side coolant hose going to the heater core at the T-fitting coming out of the firewall, being careful not to break it.
33. Remove the passenger's side coolant hose from its hardline in the general area of the heat shield using a screwdriver trick if needed.
34. [Partial] Either disconnect the brake booster line from the engine backside or remove the hose after pulling the engine out for easier access.
35. Disconnect the shifter cable by wiggling off the wide spring clip that holds it to the hanger with an adjusted lockjaw wrench.
36. Remove the bolt holding the end of the shifter cable to the shifting lever, then push the assembly forward until it pops out of the hanger.
37. [Partial] Drain the transfer case before removing the rear driveshaft from it to prevent fluid leaking from the output shaft slip yoke.
38. Depress the tab on the O2 sensor harness connector and twist a flathead screwdriver between the two harnesses to release them, then pull apart manually if needed.
39. [Partial] Remove both engine mount bolts holding the block in place.
40. [Partial] Lower the front jackstands to their lowest setting to create more lifting height for the hoist.
41. Place a floor jack under the transmission to support it and guide its movement while pulling the engine out slowly and steadily.
42. Keep the engine tilted so the block is high and the transmission/transfer case is low during the lift, constantly checking that all wires are disconnected.
43. Adjust heights back-and-forth between the engine hoist and floor jack to align them straight front-to-back as you pull the assembly out.
44. Install exhaust headers on the new VK engine with gaskets oriented so the shiny side faces inward and the black coated surface faces outward toward the headers.
45. [Partial] Clean up the VK engine block before installing it into its new home.
46. [Partial] Replace valve cover gaskets, spark plugs, and oil filter on the VK engine.
47. [Partial] Fill the VK engine with fresh oil and transmission fluid.
48. [Partial] Remove the power steering pressure sensor from behind the battery to prevent future damage during operation.
49. [Partial] Install a Frontier heater core hose fitting by replacing the stock blue-circled fitting while keeping the orange-circled hard pipe attached to it.
50. Route the VK's left-side coolant hose to the left pipe and trim several inches off the right-side hose so it fits into the right pipe.
51. Cap off the unused little nipple under the thermostat on the VK using a rubber bypass cap from a Dorman set with its own hose clamp.
52. [Partial] Vacuum pull the entire coolant system of the Xterra to remove all air pockets before adding fresh fluid.

_Procedure reported by [t286]. Photos of this job are in the source: <https://www.xterranation.org/index.php?threads/how-to-vk-swap-with-auto-trans.8909/>_

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t286] [Partial]</summary>

1. [Partial] Lift the vehicle using an engine hoist or similar method to access the underside.
2. [Partial] Locate the transmission's valve body situated above the main housing.
3. Identify bolts A, B, and C on the valve body assembly.
4. [Partial] Loosen bolt C first as it is a critical alignment point.
5. Place a container underneath the area to catch leaking fluid.
6. Remove all remaining bolts securing the valve body.
7. Support the hanging valve body with one hand while removing the final fastener.
8. Locate and disconnect the green clip near the top of the transmission housing.
9. Lower the detached valve body completely away from the engine.

</details>

## Tips & gotchas

- Fold a long cardboard piece in half to create a ramp for draining transmission fluid. [t286]
- Use a thick rag and plastic shopping bag combination when bleeding AC refrigerant to contain oily vapor. [t286]
- Stand upwind while releasing AC pressure to avoid getting sprayed. [t286]
- Refer to FSM for specific placement instructions [t286]
- Cap off a little nipple under the thermostat using a rubber bypass cap and hose clamp. [t286]
- [Partial] Vacuum pulling is guaranteed for best results; simple burping may lead to overheating during wheeling. [t286]
- Look for vendors on Facebook or Instagram specializing in these conversions. [t286]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Forgetting to vacuum-pull the coolant system before filling, leading to overheating during off-roading. [t286]
- [Partial] Destroying the power steering pressure sensor on metal overhangs behind the battery (costly replacement). [t286]
- [Partial] Pulling the wrong heater core fitting from a Frontier swap instead of keeping the stock orange-circled one. [t286]
